tools.name: inspect_source
tools.description:
Explicitly inspect provider observations to answer a numerical data question.

    This is separate from metadata search. It loads only the exact supplied
    native sources and runs read-only SQL; no discovery, proxy choice or nested
    agent is invoked. Results certify only their actual loaded source/window and
    retain native duplicates/nulls. Use selected sources and supported native
    descriptors. A metadata range alone is insufficient for a numerical answer.
    A missing or rejected descriptor is an inspection-contract limitation,
    not evidence that the source has no data. Do not guess its selectors.

handles.description: Previously returned exact native probe/inspection handles, including their explicit window. Use sources for selected native records whose descriptors have not been prepared. Barchart handles require market_source, relation_role, asset_class and target_timeframe; study_assets also requires trading_hours and roll_mode/roll_days/roll_method/nth. For Barchart, kind/category/period must be empty and revision/index_by absent. Do not guess defaults or construct selectors from loader names. Supply handles or sources, not both.
handles.title: Handles

sources.description: Copy exact owned result_ref (or retained handoff_ref) and record_ref addresses from native search, then add the explicit retrieval window. The selected record must have a compatible native dataset binding; an identity-only row is not an inspection descriptor. Backend derives provider selectors from the owned native binding; no symbol or selector guessing. Omit window only for a windowless relation. Barchart additionally needs authored market_options because metadata does not define execution/reference relation selectors. Supply sources or already-returned handles, not both.
sources.title: Sources

queries.description: Read-only SELECT queries with source-native table/column names. Omit to describe the given exact relations and a small sample first. If any source fails preparation, explicit SQL is blocked; sample the returned healthy handles before authoring new SQL.
queries.title: Queries

parameters.title: inspect_source

tools.name: build_study
tools.description: Build and save Epoch studies. New/changed definitions use study_author; operation must be exactly create, update, or clone (lowercase). For a saved-study clone use base.kind=saved_study and base.slot_id; a curated source uses base.kind=exemplar. Call only after choices/owned metadata handoff, without certifying every source fact. Each item has a caller-owned research or strategy form. For create, authoring_brief is the current self-contained objective, QA outcomes and enriched design. Update and saved-study clone carry only a self-contained change_directive. Choose the build route internally, without a reuse question. Binding selects exact prepared refs; never copy vendor/probe payloads. The author chooses source constructors and final DataOption from the brief and neutral legacy market bindings. Native source_refs instead pin the chosen dataset/schema, and an admitted universe owns the final cohort. Put authoring decision_refs in the command for audit; write their applicable values/defaults in the brief/delta. The author receives no QA ledger or original request. It does NOT interrupt. Terminal for this attempt; only the supervisor's typed recovery policy permits a retry. One studies array is a sequential batch; use it for dependent authoring operations. Independent lifecycle calls may run together on distinct outputs. RETURNS one closed BuildResult: aggregate status plus one discriminated outcome per command. Saved outcomes return the actionable logical slot_id, operation, name, form, optional final_note and mechanical validation evidence; Backend UUIDs stay in state. Preserve material validation qualifications; warnings alone do not authorize changing the requested methods. That saved slot_id is the exact logical study_slot_id consumed by run_study. The caller gives each distinct execution its own logical run_slot_id; neither tool exposes Backend UUIDs. Failed/infeasible outcomes report typed errors; author_infeasible concerns this supplied brief. Review who imposed the unmet requirement before asking. Use typed outcomes, not narration, for control flow.
